articleTitle: Rapid performance modifications to reduce prototype assessment time
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering for Time to Market
abstract: The assessment of prototypes is frequently an important stage in the introduction of new products and the speed at which it is performed can have a significant influence upon the total time and market. This has been found to be particularly true in the incorporation of embedded microprocessors in a number of industrial equipments. Of relevance in this context are equipments in which the microprocessor performs some relatively straightforward control or monitoring functions and also provides a fairly simple interface to the equipment for use by an unskilled operator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering for Time to Market
abstract: Computer Aided Software/Systems Engineering (CASE) is one of the latest approaches to solving the problems of generating software applications quickly. CASE is the automation of software engineering methods and practices, with the use of automated tools to support the creation of computer applications. The authors examine the level of life cycle support that tools provide, the methods of increasing efficiency and quality, and the benefits and problems sophisticated integrated-CASE (ICASE) tools bring. Conclusions are drawn as to whether CASE achieves the goal of speeding up software development, while still maintaining a high degree of confidence in the quality of the systems produced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Does quality in information technology cost time
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering for Time to Market
abstract: The 'time to market' for any product is clearly an important factor and even more so in a fast developing industry like Information Technology (IT). However, in addition to being quick off the mark, a successful product must also have the difficult to define attribute of quality. The rhetorical question which has prompted this paper is 'are these two objectives compatible and what are the trade offs between quality and lead time?' Supplementary questions are; can quality be guaranteed and can timescales be controlled?.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital signal processing system design methodology
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering for Time to Market
abstract: Addresses the issues of forming a structured design methodology for the development of network services and systems using digital signal processors (DSPs). The paper briefly describes the design environment for the DSP systems development process. The experiences of using one of the existing software design tools, known as Kindra, is also reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of the Yourdon structured method and the Ada language-the practical implications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering for Time to Market
abstract: Gives a brief introduction to the Yourdon Structured Method and the Ada language, describes the quality and productivity benefits gained by their use, and discusses the changes to the project management mechanisms required to successfully manage such software projects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
